title: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order $35bn of Nvidia chips, Reuters reports
content:
ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million of Nvidia’s RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards. Their combined sticker price is over $35bn. Reuters reported the orders on Tuesday, citing two people familiar with the matter. TNW has not independently verified the report.
Nvidia has told customers and partners it cannot guarantee it will fill the orders. That is according to the two sources and a third person who spoke to Reuters. Demand from Chinese tech companies far exceeds the production Nvidia has planned, they said.
Up to 10% of what was ordered
One source said Nvidia told partners they might receive only 5% to 10% of the quantities they asked for. Another said Nvidia could make no more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards worldwide in 2027. Total orders from customers in China have passed 6 million, two of the sources said.
The three companies are paying about $11,400 per card, according to two of the sources. Nvidia has told customers to expect early samples in December, with commercial deliveries from the first quarter of 2027.
Two of the sources expect Nvidia to give much of its TSMC capacity to Rubin from 2027. Rubin is its next platform for large data centres. TSMC declined to comment to Reuters.
Why a workstation card
The RTX PRO 5500 is built for powerful professional computers. It is not meant for the large data-centre clusters that run Nvidia’s top AI chips. It is still among the most powerful Nvidia chips Chinese buyers can get. US export controls bar sales of the Blackwell-based B300 to China. Washington reviews exports of the older H200 case by case.
The companies plan to use the cards mainly for inference, the three sources said. That is the work of running trained models to answer chatbot requests. Inference generally needs less computing power than training.
Last year, Chinese firms showed little interest in the RTX 6000D. Nvidia cut that similar card down to meet US rules. The firms hoped Washington would allow sales of more powerful chips. That hope has faded as the restrictions stayed and computing capacity stayed scarce, two of the sources said. Nvidia has since stopped making the RTX 6000D, and its price in China has doubled, one source said.
The orders follow a report by The Information last month that Beijing may let Alibaba and ByteDance buy the new card. Shenzhen-listed Tansun Technology said in a 13 October filing that it would buy 20,000 RTX PRO 5500 cards. It did not name the seller. It warned that shortages and overseas technology controls could delay deliveries or cut volumes.
What Nvidia says
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has said the US restrictions cut its share of China’s AI data-centre chip market. It went from a near monopoly to effectively nothing, he said. In August, the company said it expected no data-centre revenue from its first H200 shipments to China.
An Nvidia spokesperson told Reuters that Chinese makers of workstation chips and cards have seen “unprecedented growth since 2022”. That was the year the curbs began.
“US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China’s own limit on US imports,” the spokesperson said.
The curbs have pushed Chinese companies towards domestic suppliers, with Huawei gaining market share. Alibaba unveiled its Zhenwu V900 chip in September. Washington is also looking at how Chinese firms rent Nvidia chips they cannot buy.
ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent did not respond to Reuters’ requests for comment. Neither did the US Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security nor China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology.

report.summary: 字节阿里腾讯下单35亿美元英伟达GPU，供货存疑
report.background: 美国出口管制禁止英伟达对华出售Blackwell B300等顶级AI芯片，H200也需逐案审批，中国云厂商算力紧缺。RTX PRO 5500虽定位工作站，却是可合法出口到中国的较强英伟达GPU。路透社称三家巨头希望用它补足推理算力，但英伟达产能有限，且2027年台积电产能可能优先给Rubin平台。
key_points: 字节跳动、阿里巴巴和腾讯合计订购超300万张RTX PRO 5500，标价超350亿美元，单价约1.14万美元；中国客户总订单已超600万张。
英伟达告诉合作伙伴可能只能交付订单的5%至10%，2027年全球最多生产300万张；样品12月到，商业交付从2027年一季度开始。
RTX PRO 5500是工作站显卡，不是大型数据中心AI芯片，但因B300被禁、H200逐案审批，它成为中国买家能买到的最强英伟达芯片之一，主要用于推理。
去年中国企业对阉割版RTX 6000D兴趣低，期待管制放松；希望落空后算力更缺，英伟达已停产该卡，其在华价格翻倍。
管制迫使中国企业转向华为等国产供应商，阿里发布真武V900；英伟达在华数据中心份额从近垄断降至几乎为零，2027年产能还可能优先给Rubin。
report.impact: 对行业而言，中国AI推理算力短缺将持续，租赁、国产替代和灰色渠道更活跃；英伟达短期收入不确定，长期把资源押注Rubin。开发者获取高端GPU更难、成本更高，需优化推理效率并考虑国产卡或云租赁。普通用户可能面对AI服务涨价或功能受限，但短期不至于断供。
report.tools: 可关注RTX PRO 5500/Rubin路线、华为昇腾与阿里真武V900；软件侧用vLLM、SGLang、TensorRT-LLM做推理优化，并评估云GPU租赁与国产算力适配。
